title: Emrys and the Sigil
premise: Ada Yarrow has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, stealing memories from travelers to survive. When the old gods resume answering prayers, the valley's protection shatters and Ada discovers her stolen memories are the scattered pieces of a sigil that once sealed the country of Vael away from the world — a country that no longer officially exists. Hunted by the Crown's memory-eaters and guided by a disgraced priestess and a god who answers only children's prayers, Ada must reassemble the sigil and find the door out before Vael is erased entirely, taking everyone inside it with it. In the end she chooses to give up her own oldest memory — the face of the mother who abandoned her — as the final piece, sealing the door open instead of shut and founding a new home for the forgotten.
about_author: Silas Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. They write fantasy about people the records forgot, and live somewhere it rains more than it should.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Things
chapters.summary: Ada Yarrow lifts a merchant's memory of his daughter's wedding and feels, for an hour, like someone loved. POV: Ada. Establishes her gift, her loneliness, and the Hollow's strange magiclessness. Emotional beat: hunger disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Prayers in the Dark
chapters.summary: A child in the market prays aloud to a nameless god — and something answers. Candles relight; a dead bird breathes. Ada witnesses it and feels the valley's long silence crack. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: wonder edged with dread.

chapters.title: What the Valley Keeps Out
chapters.summary: Ada's fence, old Brammel, reveals the truth: the Hollow is a seal, and the gods were locked out on purpose. That night, soldiers wearing blank faces arrive asking about 'the thief who remembers.' POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the safety of home revealed as a cage.

chapters.title: The Priestess Who Fell
chapters.summary: Ada flees into the hills and is caught by Sera Ilune, a defrocked priestess who recognizes the sigil fragment glowing in Ada's stolen memories. Sera explains Vael: the country erased from every map. POV: Ada, with Sera's tale told in flashback. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: A God the Size of a Child
chapters.summary: In a ruined chapel, they meet Wren, an orphan boy whose prayers the small god Ashen still answers. Ashen speaks through Wren in riddles and demands Ada return what she stole. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: found family begins, awkward and unwanted.

chapters.title: Memory-Eaters
chapters.summary: The Crown's hunters catch their trail. One feeds on Sera's memories of her order, leaving her hollow-eyed. Ada learns the hunters want her not dead but harvested. POV: alternating Ada and a hunter, Corvane. Emotional beat: terror made personal.

chapters.title: The First Piece
chapters.summary: Ada must return a stolen memory to its dying owner — a woman who once lived in Vael — and in doing so sees the country whole: towers, festivals, a door in a mountain. POV: Ada, inside another's memory. Emotional beat: grief for a home she never had.

chapters.title: Roads That Forget Themselves
chapters.summary: The party travels toward the mountain door, but roads loop and villages deny existing. The erasure of Vael is spreading outward. Wren gets lost; Ashen goes silent. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the world itself becoming untrustworthy.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane corners Ada alone: surrender the sigil pieces and he'll restore her earliest memory — proof her mother didn't abandon her. Ada nearly takes the deal. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: temptation of a comfortable lie.

chapters.title: Sera's Confession
chapters.summary: Sera admits she helped write the original seal; she believed locking the gods out would end holy wars. Her guilt is why the hunters can track her. POV: Sera. Emotional beat: shame transformed into resolve.

chapters.title: The Market of Unclaimed Names
chapters.summary: They shelter in a hidden town of people erased by the Crown — the unrecorded, the forgotten. For one night Ada belongs somewhere. Then hunters find them. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: belonging tasted and threatened.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledger
chapters.summary: To cover the town's escape, Ada burns the Crown's census ledger, erasing herself from official record — becoming, legally, no one. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: freedom and cost entwined; justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: Wren's Prayer
chapters.summary: Wren, injured, prays desperately, and Ashen answers at full strength for the first time — revealing the god was once Vael's doorkeeper, bound and diminished. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: faith rewarded, at a price.

chapters.title: The Mountain Door
chapters.summary: They reach the door: a seam in the rock shaped exactly like the sigil. But it needs all the pieces, and two remain — one held by Corvane, one unknown even to Ashen. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into urgency.

chapters.title: What Ada Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: Ashen reveals the final piece: Ada's own first memory, taken from her so long ago she doesn't know it's missing. It holds the sigil's keystone. POV: Ada, confronting the hole in herself. Emotional beat: devastating self-recognition.

chapters.title: Corvane's Truth
chapters.summary: Corvane captures Wren. Confronting him, Ada learns he was born in Vael and serves the Crown hoping to be remembered back into existence. He isn't evil; he's terrified. POV: Corvane. Emotional beat: enemy humanized.

chapters.title: The Trade at the Threshold
chapters.summary: At the door, Corvane offers the second piece for Ada's keystone-memory — the mother, restored. Sera begs her to refuse. Ada says yes, then betrays the bargain, keeping the memory. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: choosing the many over the self.

chapters.title: The Sigil Made Whole
chapters.summary: Ada returns every stolen memory she carries, piece by piece, each one tearing something from her. The sigil blazes; the door opens onto living Vael — and onto the erasure wave closing in behind them. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: sacrifice as liberation.

chapters.title: Inside the Country That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Vael survives, half-empty, its people returning from exile and forgetting. Ashen, restored, asks Ada to be its new doorkeeper. She refuses — but proposes something better. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: exhaustion turning into vision.

chapters.title: The Door Held Open
chapters.summary: Instead of resealing, they anchor the door open using the sigil split among many keepers — Sera, Wren, the unclaimed-names town, even a repentant Corvane. No single person will carry it again. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: shared burden, true belonging.

chapters.title: The Memory She Kept
chapters.summary: Alone at last, Ada finally opens her own first memory: her mother leaving her at the Hollow's edge on purpose — to save her from Vael's fall. Grief, then forgiveness, then peace. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: the wound named and released.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: The people of Vael name their reborn country Emrys, after the child-god's oldest word for 'belonging.' Ada stays, teaching stolen memories to be given freely. A traveler arrives with nothing to steal — only a story to trade. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: home, chosen at last.
